Behavior of the common loader, reservation and crash helpers, and platform machine hooks.
Synchronization for global image pointers and entry list beyond allowance mutex and global guard.
Numeric values of capability, flag, architecture, limit, and error constants.

findings.text: Provides the reboot transition into a previously staged image. It declines when another transition holds the global guard or when no reboot image is staged, otherwise carries out preparation and hands control to the machine layer.

Reports whether the caller may stage an image of the requested kind. The decision combines a privileged capability requirement, a global disable switch, and a per-kind remaining allowance that is decremented on success.

Offers mapping of a staged segment into contiguous kernel virtual space for inspection, returning the preallocated area directly when present and otherwise gathering relevant source pages; the companion unmapping releases only vmapped ranges.

Native load entry validates request parameters and architecture selection, duplicates the caller segment descriptions into kernel memory, invokes the common loader, then frees the duplicate and returns the outcome.

Compatibility load entry performs the same high level validation but rejects default architecture selection, translates each compat descriptor field by field into native form, then delegates to the common loader.

Restart preparation notifies registered listeners, marks system state as restarting, blocks further helper spawning and shuts devices; CPU migration pins the caller to the designated reboot processor after ensuring it is online.

Initialization creates a kexec object under the kernel object, attaches attribute groups, then creates legacy alias links best effort while reporting failures without aborting; a separate early hook registers the kernel controls.
All segment loaders choose the data origin from an in-kernel buffer when file-backed mode is active and from caller memory otherwise, tracking remaining supplied and required lengths independently.

Normal loading records the destination once, then iterates over required length page by page, clearing each fresh page, copying at most the available supplied portion, advancing both addresses, and cooperatively yielding.

Crash loading writes directly to the boot physical destination page for each step, zeroes any trailing portion beyond supplied data, flushes instruction cache visibility, and balances platform alloc and free hooks around the mapping.

Contiguous preallocated loading copies linearly through the reserved area without allocating pages or recording entries, yielding periodically; the routine attempts to clear trailing space after the loop.

The image records an ordered list of tagged destinations and sources terminated by an empty slot. Alignment to page boundary is enforced before tagging, and exhaustion of the current table links a newly allocated table through indirection.

Page allocation preserves the rule that a source page either coincides with its own destination or is not a destination at all. It reuses queued destination matches, diverts over-limit pages to an unusable list, skips live destination ranges, and may exchange contents with an existing association to free a usable page.

Destination usage lookup walks the recorded sequence remembering the most recent destination tag and reports the source slot whose associated destination equals the queried page, otherwise reports absence.

Load validation proceeds in order: privileged permission including allowance accounting, mandatory access and integrity mediation, lockdown mediation, legality of flag combination reserving room for extensions, and an upper bound on segment count.

Readouts report boolean presence of reboot and crash images, current crash reservation size, contiguous ranges line by line, and core header size. The size control also accepts a numeric write to attempt shrinking the reservation and echoes the written length on success.

ELF recognition compares the leading identification bytes against the expected magic sequence. Numeric field conversion selects little endian, big endian or unchanged interpretation according to the encoding byte in the identification.

Two global pointers hold the staged reboot and crash images, a boolean tracks whether a transition is underway, a debug flag controls extra file logging, and an integer disables further loads once set.
Both core and ELF components prepend a fixed module tag to diagnostic messages.
Each load allowance counter is guarded by its own mutex. The initial unlimited marker is never decremented, zero denies further loads, and concurrent check and control paths serialize updates.
A global atomic guard serializes execution of the reboot transition; the transition path acquires it at entry and releases on all exits, reporting busy when already held.
The allowance object pairs a mutual exclusion primitive with a signed integer count, where a negative sentinel denotes no enforcement and non-negative values denote remaining permitted loads.
The compatibility link descriptor pairs two character string references, one identifying the existing attribute target and one identifying the legacy alias exposed at the parent.

Reboot execution branches on context preservation. The preserving branch freezes user activity, suspends consoles and devices in staged order, quiesces secondary processors and core subsystems, then reverses those stages after control returns. The normal branch flags progress, prepares restart, migrates processor, shuts core services, re-enables hotplug, announces start and shuts the machine before handing off.

The allowance control accepts only non-negative writes and only decreases a currently enforced value; reading returns the current count under guard. The global disable control permits only a one way change from enabled to disabled.

Callers observe permission denial for unprivileged or disallowed loads, invalid argument for illegal flags or architecture or excess segments, memory exhaustion when page allocation fails, and fault indication when caller data cannot be transferred.
Segment mapping may return no mapping when auxiliary array allocation or virtual mapping fails, logging a diagnostic; it warns if fewer pages than expected were collected for the requested range.
The sentinel denoting absence of a destination equals the maximum unsigned long value with all bits set.

Stable user visible names include kernel controls for load disable and per-kind limits and a kexec directory exposing loaded status, crash status, crash size, contiguous ranges and core header size plus legacy aliases at the parent.
